newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dlr edges ahead on hope of steady policy.
newsitem.headline: Australia dlr edges ahead on hope of steady policy.

text.p: The Australian dollar pushed cautiously higher Wednesday as the market became a little more confident the Reserve Bank would not ease policy near term.

Bulls won early relief from rate tension when the RBA let its 9.30 am operation pass with no move, confounding those who thought it would cut at the first opportunity following its monthly board meeting on Tuesday.

And data on retail sales and the housing sector, while mixed, had enough surface strength to swing waverers into the steady policy camp. The upbeat tempo was rounded off by a positive assessment on Australia from rating agency Moody's.
By 5.30 pm (0730 GMT) the local dollar had staged a careful rally to US$0.7547/52 having eased to US$0.7510/15 at the opening from US$0.7525/30 late here Tuesday.
Traders said the break baove US$0.7540 resistance boded well for the currency and a further short covering push to US$0.7575 was possible tonight.

Further gains would probably have to wait until Thursday when, if all went to plan, both the RBA and the Federal Reserve would confirm market expectations and leave their respective rates steady. In such case there would be scope to top 76 cents, although most thought US$0.7630 resistance beyond it.
This was a considerable turnaround from just last Friday when the currency had delved as deep as US$0.7440, a 17-month low, as the market succumbed to fears the RBA would soon ease.
Today's events convinced many the bank was on hold for now and and would absorb key inflation and wages data on July 23/24 before deciding whether another move was needed.

One reason was a sterling 2.9 percent rise in retail sales for May, the largest gain since March 1994 and at the very top end of market forecasts. The bounce was all the more imortant as it was a shock 1.7 percent drop in sales in April which first started the market thinking about a fifth cut in official rates.
